missionPremise: TWO OPERATOR RULINGS, 2026-08-19, both surfaced by executors rather than by the planner and both taken to the operator before this lane existed. (1) `template-city` read `0 of 10 sources granted` in the nav footer while three regions rendered populated fixture data. Every word was true - `fixtureGrants` is a demonstration axis that names adapter kinds, carries no `sourceUrl`, and connects nothing, so the granted count is genuinely zero - but a prospect reads a contradiction. The ruling is DISTINGUISH, not collapse: a granted source and a demonstrated shape are different claims and the footer must say which is which, with `grantedAdapters` staying `[]` on every pack and `assertCityPackShape` keeping its `a pack that generates fixtures grants no adapter` guard. Source: the T1PACK close's own open question, `_inbox/2026-08-19_t1pack_close.json` whatRemainsOpen[5]. (2) The Connections register row `Auth / session / notifications / theme / sign out` bundles four jobs, and after G-90 two exist and two do not; with the disposition vocabulary CLOSED at six values no single value is true of the row as written, which is why the G-90 lane deliberately did not edit it and routed a ruling instead. The ruling is SPLIT: each job gets its own row with its own honest disposition, and the second flagged row `Feedback with screenshot and category` gets the same treatment. Source: `_inbox/2026-08-19_t1shell_close.json` openItems, `Two Connections register rows are now partly false`. Both rest on the deeper 2026-08-19 operator ruling in `_inbox/2026-08-19_template_city_lens_build_sheet.md`: honest absence is a statement about SOURCES, not about screens, and the product must be able to say which.
completionPredicate: A stranger can evaluate this without me by running six things. (1) `node --test src/*.test.mjs` in the clone returns 277/277, against 273/273 on the base SHA. (2) `GET /api/city-identity?cityKey=template-city` returns a `sources` block carrying BOTH `0 of 10 sources granted` and `2 of 10 demonstrated with fixture records`, each with its own counting rule, and `GET .../empty-city` returns `0 of 10 demonstrated with fixture records` with the positive-determination rule `this pack generates no records, so no adapter kind is demonstrated on it`. (3) Neither figure is hardcoded: moving the catalog or the pack's grants in a scratch copy moves the numbers with `src/city-identity.mjs`, `web/index.html` and `web/app.js` sha256-identical across every arm. (4) `GET /?work=connections` serves 75 register rows, of which seven are the split rows, each with a disposition drawn from the unchanged six-value vocabulary, and the panel head reads `70 of 70` and `from 67 Homes-table rows`. (5) `G-88 the bake is fresh / leaves web/index.html unchanged when the bake is run again` is green, and was watched failing by name on three separate planted hand edits before being restored byte-identically by running the bake. (6) The CI check-run conclusion STRING on the head SHA is `success` and PR 29 is OPEN and unmerged. All six are recorded below with raw output.
scopeBasis: IN, and why. Both operator-ruled corrections in full, because the dispatch names them as shapes to implement rather than judgement calls to re-open. The two derived footer figures and their two counting rules, in `packSources()` - the SAME resolver that already derives the granted figure - because a second resolver is the CTRL-1 shape this repo has paid for and DEV_PROCESS 2.4 forbids. The seven split register rows plus the `splitFrom` field and the measured source-row count, because the dispatch requires the counting rule and any test pinning it to move with the split. Baking the Connections panel-head figures and the counting-rule caption, because they were three HAND-TYPED copies of a rule that lives in the generator and a split that changes the row count is exactly the edit that leaves them stale - this is not scope creep away from G-93, it is the only way to state the new count on the page without hand-typing it, which the dispatch forbids for the footer figure and which would be no more defensible here. OUT, and deliberately so. `web/sc-kit.css`, forbidden by the dispatch and by the cross-repo byte-identity rule. Anything under `src/domains/`, plus `src/domains.mjs`, `src/fixture-seam.mjs` and `src/adapters.mjs`, which are the two live sibling lanes' territory and were verified against their dispatches at source before any file was opened. The disposition VOCABULARY, which stays closed at six because the ruling was that no single value was true of a BUNDLE, not that the vocabulary was short - and all seven split rows were expressible within it. Any per-region rendering of the four source states, which is a separate lens pass. Merging and deploying, both planner-owned. NOT out of scope but NOT DONE, stated so it is not mistaken for an exclusion: the footer is proven by served bytes and by the resolved payload, never by a browser, so how tall the two-figure chip sits in a real 248px sidebar is unverified; and the register's disposition column remains HAND-DECLARED, so the seven declarations are honest today and nothing derives them from the built surface.

whatRemainsOpen: PR 29 is OPEN and MERGEABLE on head 7820746 with CI conclusion string `success`. This lane does not merge and did not deploy. CODE-DONE IS NOT CUSTOMER-DONE: nothing here has been seen on the deployed surface.

THE FOOTER IS PROVEN BY BYTES, NOT BY A BROWSER. The two figures and two rules are verified in the served document and in the resolved payload. `.nav-foot .prov` already wraps (flex-wrap, white-space normal, row-gap) so the added content wraps inside the existing chip rather than overflowing, but how tall the chip sits in a real 248px sidebar is a rendered check. CI is a bare Node image and a test that silently skips when a browser is absent is a control that never fires, so this belongs with whoever next runs a real browser against the deployed surface. Stated rather than implied.

THE REGISTER'S DISPOSITION COLUMN IS STILL HAND-DECLARED. Splitting made these seven declarations honest today; nothing derives any disposition from the built surface, so the column can drift again exactly as it did between G-73 and G-90. Deriving it is a larger change than this card and was deliberately not smuggled in.

The G-18 source file `_inbox/2026-08-17_g18_shell_homes.md` still carries the two bundled rows as single rows. The register now says 67 source rows and 70 register rows and names the split per row, so the two are reconcilable rather than silently divergent - but if the source file is ever re-derived from the register, the counting rule must travel with it.

The three new footer/panel ids are static markup that no served script reads (connections-rows, connections-rows-rule, connections-addenda, connections-addenda-rule, connections-counting-rule). That matches the existing precedent of connections-sources, which is also baked and never addressed, but it means the addressability gate does not watch them; the bake fixed-point assertion is what watches them instead.
